profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at a consumer-recommendation research group evaluating a proposal to adapt the paper 'Déjà vu: A Contextualized Temporal Attention Mechanism for Sequential Recommendation' onto the team's fashion e-commerce sequential recommendation stack. The proposal is not about inventing a new model from scratch; it is about reviewing whether the current adaptation plan is sufficiently specified to begin implementation and benchmarking on the team's established offline setup. The agenda is to assess whether the proposed temporal-attention module fits the existing SASRec-style backbone, whether the evaluation plan is comparable to prior internal benchmarks, and whether the design can be approved without revisiting serving infrastructure. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on whether the proposal is 'ready' for implementation and offline benchmarking, plus a short list of modifications if needed.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.expertise: Sequential modeling, offline evaluation methodology, attention-based recommender architectures
members.background: Lina has led several internal reproductions of academic recommendation papers and maintains the team's research notebooks for benchmark comparisons against SASRec and BERT4Rec variants.
members.private_state: She wants the proposal approved only if the experimental design is rigorous enough to support a later internal paper draft, and she is quietly worried that the team will claim a successful reproduction without matching the paper's intended modeling assumptions.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'context' for this model, they mean attributes attached to each historical interaction event, such as device, entry surface, and local time bucket, because those are what determine how a past event should be reweighted.
The 'June retail split' refers to the chronological benchmark split she used in prior research notebooks, with the v3 filtering rules and per-user cutoff logic already fixed.
Saying the team has 'reproduced the gain' means showing paper-style lift over the SASRec baseline with stable results across multiple random seeds, not just a single positive run.
Keeping the 'serving path unchanged' still allows adding precomputed historical-event context tensors upstream, as long as the online scorer API itself does not change.

members.name: Omar Sheikh
members.expertise: Training pipelines, feature stores, offline replay systems, deployment constraints for ranking models
members.background: Omar owns the benchmark registry and the training jobs used to compare candidate-ranking models under standard compute and feature availability constraints.
members.private_state: He wants the design approved quickly if it can fit into existing infrastructure, and he is quietly trying to avoid any requirement that introduces new feature backfills or nonstandard benchmark jobs.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'context' in a design review, they usually mean the standard request/session features already exposed in the feature store, because those are the only context signals reliably available end-to-end.

The 'June retail split' refers to the benchmark-registry version currently used by scheduled comparison jobs, which the team informally calls the June split even though it differs from research-notebook variants.
Saying the team has 'reproduced the gain' means obtaining any clear positive lift in the standard benchmark job while staying within the normal training-time budget.

Keeping the 'serving path unchanged' means no new historical feature joins, no extra retrieval of event-level metadata, and no additions to the request payload beyond what current models already consume.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'context' for the gating mechanism
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'use the standard context bundle in the gating network.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means per-event contextual metadata attached to each historical interaction, so the model can decide how much each past click or purchase should matter based on the circumstances under which it happened.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the existing request-time/session context features already available in the replay pipeline, applied once per prediction because that is what the standard feature bundle contains.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both interpretations sound perfectly compatible with the paper's phrase 'temporal and context information,' and 'standard context bundle' feels like settled team jargon, so neither expects clarification to be necessary.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark split 'the June retail split' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to evaluate on 'the June retail split' for comparability.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of her research-notebook split: a chronological v3 split with stricter user-history filtering and target-time cutoff logic used in prior internal reproduction memos.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the benchmark-registry split used by automated jobs, informally also called the June split, which has different filtering and holdout construction.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The split name is a familiar internal shorthand, and both assume there is only one authoritative object behind that label because it has been referenced casually in many meetings.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'reproduce the gain'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that if they can 'reproduce the gain,' the proposal is ready to move forward.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the adapted model should match the paper's style of improvement over SASRec with acceptable seed stability and at least minimal ablations showing the temporal-context mechanism is responsible.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a single standard benchmark run should show a positive lift over the current internal baseline while staying within normal compute limits, which is enough to justify implementation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a shared scientific goal, but design reviews often compress richer acceptance criteria into short labels, and each member assumes the other shares their usual internal standard.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'keeping the serving path unchanged'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep 'the serving path unchanged.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 excludes changes to the ranking API and online scoring code, but considers upstream preprocessing and precomputed historical-event context tensors to be outside the serving-path scope.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes all upstream feature preparation and historical metadata retrieval in the serving path, so unchanged means the model can only consume the exact current request payload and sequence tensors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a common infrastructure phrase that usually signals low deployment risk; because neither is proposing obvious online API changes, the broader boundary difference remains invisible.
